info.title: Decryptx External Api
info.description:
# Overview
The purpose of the Decryptx management APIs are to provide Decryptx
Partners and Key Injection Facilities (KIFs) a way to integrate their services
to the Decryptx Platform. These APIs allow them to integrate P2PE Manager functionality into
their own services, therefore providing their merchants an alternative to
the P2PE Manager for common tasks.

### Deleting Resource
With the Management APIs, as with the P2PE Manager, once a resource has been utilized it cannot be deleted. For example, if a user has logged into the system even once they cannot be deleted. Instead of deleting resources that have been deleted, they shhould be set to inactive.

### Transactions endpoints
The transaction endpoints are included in the Management APIs for Partners that have their own (Domain 5) P2PE compliant decryption environment and who wish to use our platform to manage their partners, merchants and devices. Our transactions endpoints allow Partners journal their decryption activity into the P2PE Manager, allowing the Partner to utilize the device management and chain-of-custody functionality of the P2PE Manager. Even when decryptions occur outside of the Decryptx system, the Partner's Client can still benefit from the P2PE Manager's device management, chain of custody, and historical decryption activity logs functionality.

# Authentication
All calls to our Management APIs support basic and HMAC authentication. For instruction of how to implement HMAC please refer to the guide on our developer portal (https://developers.bluefin.com/p2pe-manager/apiguides/hmac).

Basic authentication is a simple authentication scheme built into the HTTP protocol, the client sends HTTP requests with an Authorization header that contains the word *'Basic'*, followed by a space and a base64-encoded string username:password. For example, for the username and password, user and password, the authentication header is as follows:
~~~
//Authorization: Basic base64(user:pasword)
~~~
Output:
~~~
Authorization: Basic dXNlcjpwYXNzd29yZA==
~~~
The Management accept the same usernames and passwords from the P2PEManager; importantly, access to respourse are limited based on the user role. A KIF user can access number of API endpoints that the Patner user cannot and vice versa. On the other hand, there are a number of APIs that are common to both types of Users.


### Partner User Access
The following table outlines the REST operations that a Partner user can access. Client level users are not allowed to integrate with theses APIs, instead these APIs are designed so that the Client's Partner would integrate functionality to their service. That design decision has resulted in the Partners having increased access to P2PE resources on the APIs when compared to the P2PEManager GUI. For example, a Partner can alter a device's state with the Management APIs, whereas they cannot on the P2PE Manager GUI.

| EndPoint             | GET (all) | POST | GET (Single) | PATCH | DELETE |
|----------------------|:---------:|:----:|:------------:|:-----:|:------:|
| /api/v1/users        |     ✔     |   ✔  |       ✔      |   ✔   |   ✔*   |
| /api/v1/partners     |     ✔     |   ✔  |       ✔      |   ✔   |        |
| /api/v1/clients      |     ✔     |   ✔  |       ✔      |   ✔   |        |
| /api/v1/decryption   |           |   ✔  |              |       |        |
| /api/v1/devices      |     ✔     |   ✔  |       ✔      |   ✔   |   ✔*   |
| /api/v1/deviceBuilds |     ✔     |      |       ✔      |       |        |
| /api/v1/deviceTypes  |     ✔     |      |       ✔      |       |        |
| /api/v1/deviceStates |     ✔     |      |              |       |        |
| /api/v1/devices/{serial}/{type}/custody  |     ✔     |   ✔   |       ✔      |       |        |
| /api/v1/locations    |     ✔     |   ✔  |       ✔      |   ✔   |   ✔*   |
| /api/v1/shipments    |           |      |              |       |        |
| /api/v1/attestations |     ✔     |   ✔  |       ✔      |       |        |
| /api/v1/transactions |     ✔     |   ✔  |       ✔      |   ✔   |        |
| /api/v1/kifs         |     ✔     |      |              |       |        |
| /api/v1/injectkeys   |           |      |              |       |        |
| /api/v1/virtualDevices/{partner}   |           |   ✔   |       ✔       |       |    ✔    |
* A resource that has been used one or more times cannot be deleted.


### KIF User Access
The following table outlines the subset of Management APIs that a KIF user can access. Within this subset, some resources will only appear if they are in a particular state. For example, a Device will appear in the GET all endpoint if its deviceState is set to Unassigned, Assigned, or Injected. Once it is received by the merchant and set to *'stored'* or *'activating'* it will no longer appear on the GET all devices response for the originating KIF.


| Endpoint             | GET (all) | POST | GET (Single) | PATCH | DELETE |
|----------------------|:---------:|:----:|:------------:|:-----:|:------:|
| /api/v1/users        |     ✔     |   ✔  |       ✔      |   ✔   |   ✔*   |
| /api/v1/partners     |     ✔     |      |       ✔      |       |        |
| /api/v1/clients      |     ✔     |      |       ✔      |       |        |
| /api/v1/decryption   |           |   ✔  |              |       |        |
| /api/v1/devices      |     ✔     |   ✔  |       ✔      |       |        |
| /api/v1/deviceBuilds |     ✔     |      |       ✔      |       |        |
| /api/v1/deviceTypes  |     ✔     |      |       ✔      |       |        |
| /api/v1/deviceStates |     ✔     |      |              |       |        |
| /api/v1/devices/{serial}/{type}/custody  |           |       |              |       |        |
| /api/v1/locations    |     ✔     |   ✔  |       ✔      |   ✔   |   ✔*   |
| /api/v1/shipments    |     ✔     |   ✔  |       ✔      |   ✔   |        |
| /api/v1/attestations |           |      |              |       |        |
| /api/v1/transactions |           |      |              |       |        |
| /api/v1/kifs         |     ✔     |      |              |       |        |
| /api/v1/injectkeys   |     ✔     |      |       ✔      |       |        |
| /api/v1/virtualDevices/{partner}   |           |       |               |       |         |
* A resource that has been used one or more times it cannot be deleted.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: The User APIs are used by both KIFs and Partners to manage their users. The APIs allow them to create, read, update, and delete Users. Partners can also manage Users on behalf of their Clients.

tags.name: Devices
tags.description: Devices are P2PE enabled Payment terminals and card readers. Typically, Devices are added by the KIF user. Once they have injected them with a key, they are shipped to the Client.

tags.name: Partners
tags.description: Partners are an entity that refers, sets up, or supports clients who are processing on Bluefin’s P2PE platform. A Partner could be Software Provider, a merchant account sales office, a payment gateway, or a reseller of payment gateway. A Sub Partner account can be used as an organization construct to group Clients. For example, a Partner may want to create a (sub) Partner to group together 10 Clients so they are grouped for reporting purposes.

tags.name: Clients
tags.description: Clients are merchants who process P2PE transactions. Our Clients APIs allow a Partner to create, read, update and delete their clients. While it is not possible for a Client to integrate with these Management APIs themselves, they can manage shipping, devices, and attestations through the P2PE Manager GUI application. KIF users can read (GET) Clients, however only Partner users can create and alter (POST and PATCH) them.

tags.name: Locations
tags.description: According to PCI rules a record of every P2PE Device must be kept as it is shipped to a Person at a Location. Our set of Location APIs allow a Partner to manage Locations for their Clients. Depending on how a Partner want, their reporting and access control organised, they can set up a Client to can have multiple Locations or they can create a Client per location.

tags.name: Shipments
tags.description: In order to adhere to PCI rules, the shipment of P2PE Devices from the KIF to the Client must be logged and tracked. Our Shipment APIs allow a KIF and Partner user record their Shipments.

tags.name: Attestations
tags.description: The attestations APIs allow a Partner to manage the on-site PCI DSS compliance assessments on behalf of their Clients. The Partner can create and read attestations through the API. Attestations cannot be deleted. Kif users do not have permission to access the Attestation.

tags.name: Transactions
tags.description: The transaction endpoints are included in the Management APIs for Partners that have their own (Domain 5) P2PE compliant decryption environment and who wish to use our platform to manage their partners, merchants and devices. Our transactions endpoints allow Partners journal their decryption activity on the P2PE Manager.

tags.name: Inject Keys
tags.description: Decryptx supports a number of P2PE (and non-P2PE) keys. When creating a Device, it is important that a KIF user tracks the key that is injected. Therefore, we we provide two read only API endpoints that list them for KIF users. One will return a list of decryption keys and the other will return the complete details from an individual device.

tags.name: Device Types
tags.description: In order to create a Device, it must contain a reference to a Device Type resource. The Device Type APIs list the supported device types. The information available includes the name of the Device manufacturer and the device model.

tags.name: Device States
tags.description: The Device States API list the supported state names and their ID.

tags.name: Device Builds
tags.description: The Device Builds API list the supported device builds. When creating a Device entry a Device Build must be specified.

tags.name: Device Custody
tags.description: The Device Custody APIs allow a Partner update a Device's location and custodian.

tags.name: Kifs
tags.description: The KIF APIs list the registered KIFs and their ID.

tags.name: Virtual Devices
tags.description: Virtual Devices are Devices that a Partner shared with another Partner.

get.description: This endpoint returns a summarised list of all Users assigned to a Partner's account. To view a User's complete dataset, a call must be made to the get a single User endpoint. By default, Users from sub-partner accounts are automatucally included. A partner can lookup a Client's Users by including the client id or name as a request parameter. Other filters will limit the Users in the response by Partner or KIF. Use the *'skip'* and *'take'* parameters to implement pagination.

parameters.name: partner
parameters.description: Filter the list by Partner. The parameter value can be either the Partner's ID or Name.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: Filter the list by Client. The parameter value can be either the Client's ID or Name.

parameters.name: kif
parameters.description: Filter the list by KIF. The parameter value can be either the KIF's ID or Name.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: The number of entries to include in the list.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The number of results to skip before listing entries.

post.description: This endpoint creates a User for either a Partner, a KIF, or a Client. To create a User for a KIF, a reference to the KIF must be included in the API call, to create a user for a Client, both the Partner and Client references must be included.

get.description: This endpoint returns an object that contains all the User's details.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The User's unique identifier.

delete.description: This endpoint deletes a User resource. Deleting User reources is only possible if the User has not logged into the P2PE Manger. If the User resource is sucessfully deleted the response body will contain an empty object.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the User to delete.

patch.description: This endpoint updates an existing User resource. It is not neccessary to include the complete replacement object in the API call; an object containing the properties that are to be changed will suffice.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the User to update.

requestBody.description: The User resource to be updated.

get.description: This endpoint returns a list of Shipments.

That can only be performed on the P2PE Manager GUI.

get.description:
This endpoint returns a list of Transactions. The list can be filtered by a number of Transaction properties.

By default the paging.mode is set to nocount, this means that the list total count will not be included in the response. Setting the paging.mode parameter to full will enable the total count. However, we urge Partners to exercise caution when including the total count on the Transaction list endpoint. The total number of Transactions can grow significantly and counting them can become taxing on the system. Paging.mode full is likely to result in high latency, therefore we suggest that you adopt a pagination strategy that does not require the total count.

parameters.name: partner
parameters.description: Filter the list by Partner. The parameter value can be either a Partner ID or Name.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: Filter the list by Client. The parameter value can be either a Client ID or Name.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Filter the list by Location. The parameter value can be either a Location ID or Name.

parameters.name: success
parameters.description: Filter the list by success indicator.

parameters.name: dateFrom
parameters.description: Filter the list by transaction date. Only show transactions that were processed after this date.

parameters.name: dateTo
parameters.description: Filter the list by transaction date. Only show transactions that were processed before this date.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: Filter the list by Message ID.

parameters.name: clientRef
parameters.description: Filter the list by the ClientRef ID.

parameters.name: serialNumber
parameters.description: Filter the list by Device serial number.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Filter the list by Reference ID.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: The number of entries to include in the list.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The number of results to skip before listing entries.

parameters.name: paging.mode
parameters.description: Toggles the total count in the response.

post.description: This endpoint creates a Transaction. It should only be used when decryption activity occurs outside of the Decryptx platform. Certain Partners may operate their own Validated P2PE decryption environment (Domain 5). This allows the partner to journal their decryption activity into the P2PE Manager, allowing the Partner to utilize the P2PE Manager for their device management and chain of custody. The Partner's Client can still benefit from the device management, chain of custody, and historical decryption activity even when decryptions occur outside of the Decryptx system.

get.description: Return information about a specific decryption record.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Transaction's unique identifier.

parameters.name: id

get.description:
This endpoint returns a list of Devices. This endpoint can be returned. Some Devices will only appear for certain types of Users if they are in a particular state. For example, when a KIF user makes this API call, a Device will be included in the response list if its deviceState is set to *'Unassigned'*, *'Assigned'*, or *'Injected'*. Once it is received by the merchant and its deviceState is set to *'Stored'* or *'Activating'*, the Device will no longer appear on the GET all devices response for the KIF user.

The list of Devices can be filtered by the Partner, Client, KIF, and the Device's state. Use the *'skip'* and *'take'* parameters to implement pagination.

parameters.name: partner
parameters.description: Filter the list by Partner. The parameter value can be either a Partner ID or Name.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: Filter the list by Client. The parameter value can be either a Client ID or Name.

parameters.name: kif

parameters.name: serialNumber
parameters.description: Filter the list by a comma separated list of serial numbers.

parameters.name: deviceState
parameters.description: Filter the list by Device State.

parameters.name: take

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The number of results to skip before listing entries.

parameters.name: sorting.field
parameters.description: The field to order the Device list.

parameters.name: sorting.direction
parameters.description: The direction to sort the Device list.

post.description: This endpoint creates a Device. Due to the chain-of-custody rules Devices are typically created by the KIF user. The serial number of the device, the device type, the Partner, the Client, the injection key, and the firmware can be specified at device creation.

get.summary: Get a Device by Serial & Type

It is not neccessary to include the complete replacement object in the API call; an object containing the properties that are to be changed will suffice. For example, this endpoint can be used to change a Device's state from 'injected' to 'inTransit'.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Device's unique identifier.

PartnerReference.description: Reference to the associated Partner. When used for POST and PATCH API calls, the reference can contain either the ID or Name. With GET API calls, both properties are populated.

PartnerReferenceRoot.description: Reference to the Client's root Partner. The Client's direct Partner is a Sub-Partner of this root Partner. The root and direct Partner's can be the same resource.

ClientReference.description: Reference to the associated Client resource. When used for POST and PATCH API calls, the reference can contain either the ID or Name. With GET API calls, both properties are populated.

KifReference.description: Reference to the associated KIF resource. When used for POST and PATCH API calls, the reference can contain either the ID or Name. With GET API calls, both properties are populated.

LocationReference.description: Reference to the associated Location resource. When used for POST and PATCH API calls, the reference can contain either the ID or Name. With GET API calls, both properties are populated.

customReference.description: A custom refernce to location object. This value can be set

LocationWithCustomReference.description: Reference to the associated Location resource. When used for POST and PATCH API calls, the reference can contain either the ID or Name. With GET API calls, both properties are populated.

UserReference.description: Reference to the associated User resource. When used for POST and PATCH API calls, the reference must contain the User's id.

UserReferenceDetailed.description: Reference to the associated User resource. When used for POST and PATCH API calls, the reference must contain the User's id.

UserDetailsReference.description: Reference to the associated User resource.

UserRoleReference.description: Reference to the associated User Role.

DeviceTypeReference.description: Reference to the associated Device Type resource. When used for POST and PATCH API calls, the reference can contain either the ID or Name. With GET API calls, both properties are populated.

DeviceStateReference.description: Reference to the associated Device State resource. When used for POST and PATCH API calls, the reference can contain either the ID or Name. With GET API calls, both properties are populated.

code.description: The referenced Country's code (two uppercase symbols).

CountryReference.description: Reference to the associated Country. When used for POST and PATCH API calls, the reference can contain either the ISO-ALPHA2 country Code or Name.

DeviceReference.description: Reference to the associated Device resource. When used for POST and PATCH API calls, the reference can contain either the ID or Serial Number. With GET API calls, both properties are included in the response.

DeviceBuildReference.description: Reference to the associated Device Build resource. When used for POST and PATCH API calls, the reference can contain either the ID or Name. With GET API calls the id, name and build number are included in the response.

InjectKeyReference.description: Reference to the associated Device resource. When used for POST and PATCH API calls, the reference can contain either the ID or Name. With GET API calls, both properties are included in the response.

CreateResult.description: A simple object containing the ID of the newly created resource.

id.description: The unique identifier of the updated resource

message.description: Human readable description of the error message.

message.description: Human readable description of the error message.

sequenceNumber.description: Sequence number obtained from device in base 64 or hex encoded format. This value is typically required for DUKPT encryption/decryption. This parameter is optional and not required if the device does not generate a key sequence number.

reference.description: A string (of up to 50 characters) that helps partners identify individual API calls. If provided, the value will be logged to the P2PE Manager where it can be used to troubleshoot technical issues. It is highly recommended that a unique value be used on each Decryptx API call. The reference value will be returned in the response body, whether the API call is successful or not.

cbcVector.description: Base64 or hex encoded initial vector obtained from device. This parameter is optional. It’s used in devices that implement 3DES Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) encryption with non-zero initial vector.

hasCcData.description: Validation flag that indicates whether inbound and outbound data should be checked for credit card numbers. If hasCcData is set to "1" and the inbound data contains a credit card number or if the outbound data does not contain credit card number the decrypt operation will fail. If hasCcData is set to "0", no checks will be performed on inbound and outbound data. If no value for hasCcData flag provided, Decryptx defaults it to "1".

name.description: String identifier for the value to be decrypted. This name will be returned in the response so that values can be matched up. Additionally, the response array of decrypted values will be returned in the same order they were provided.

value.description: Base64 or hex encoded encrypted data retrieved from device.

success.description: true if the payload decryption was successful.
